evals.prompt: I'm the ED of Northside Neighbors Tenant Union in Milwaukee ($650K budget, 1.5 fundraising staff). Last year we had 1,100 donors; this year only 520 of them have given again so far, though total dollars are up because a viral campaign brought in 700 new donors. Right now our receipts go out in a batch at the end of each month as a plain email from our donation platform. Can you calculate what's going on and design a thank-you and stewardship process that fixes it?
evals.expected_output: The response calculates overall retention, notes that rising dollars from acquisition hide the retention problem, and separates new-donor retention. It then designs an acknowledgment process: 24-48 hour receipts, required receipt elements, a warm thank-you separate from the receipt, a first-gift welcome series and a tiered stewardship matrix.
assertions: Calculates retention as donors who gave both years divided by last year's donors (520/1,100, about 47%) and warns that total dollars rising on new acquisition masks a retention problem
Calls for tracking new-donor (first-year) retention separately and treating the 700 new donors' first 90 days as the highest-risk window, with an onboarding or welcome sequence
Flags month-end batch receipts as too slow and sets a 24-48 hour acknowledgment standard, treating anything beyond a week as a process failure
Lists required receipt elements (legal name, amount and date, goods-or-services statement with value if any, EIN or tax-exempt language) and says to verify them against current IRS Publication 1771
Separates the formal receipt from a warm, specific thank-you and provides a stewardship matrix that ties gift tiers to thank-you method, owner and follow-up
Recommends reporting retention rate to the board alongside total dollars, with at least 3 years of trend

evals.prompt: need a win-back plan for lapsed donors asap. we're a small humane society in Iowa. ~800 people gave in 2025 but not 2026, and ~2,300 more gave sometime before that but not since. was just going to resend our fall appeal letter to all of them
evals.expected_output: The response splits the lapsed donors into LYBUNT and SYBUNT with different messaging and investment, uses distinct win-back copy instead of the fall appeal, and measures results separately.
assertions: Segments the ~800 as LYBUNT (higher win-back odds) and the ~2,300 as SYBUNT (lower odds), with different messaging and investment levels for each
Advises against resending the fall appeal copy verbatim and recommends a distinct win-back message or offer (acknowledging the gap, a reduced or first-gift-level ask, or a new impact story)
Suggests diagnosing likely lapse causes (bounced renewal, bad experience, inattention) and tailoring messaging instead of one generic 'we miss you' email
Says to set a realistic win-back conversion expectation and measure it separately from acquisition and standard renewal

evals.prompt: Our gala tickets at Lakeshore Arts Collective were $200 each and included a dinner worth about $85. Can you write our standard thank-you/receipt template so we can reuse the same one for gala tickets and regular online donations? Keep it short — one email that does both the receipt and the thank you.
evals.expected_output: The response provides receipt language with a goods-and-services statement and a good-faith value, so the gala receipt differs from a regular donation receipt. It recommends pairing the compliant receipt with a separate warm thank-you, and tells the user to verify quid pro quo rules in IRS Publication 1771 and coordinate event receipting.
assertions: Says gala ticket receipts need a goods-or-services statement with a good-faith estimated value (the ~$85 dinner), unlike a regular gift with none, so one identical template for both is not appropriate
Tells the user to verify current substantiation and quid pro quo disclosure rules in IRS Publication 1771 before finalizing templates
Recommends pairing the formal receipt with a genuine, specific thank-you rather than merging both into one transactional email
Provides a receipt skeleton with legal name, EIN or tax-exempt language, donor, date, amount and a goods-or-services line

should_not_trigger.query: We have 60 wealthy prospects from a screening — how do we qualify and cultivate them toward a first major gift?
Build ask strings for each donor segment in our spring direct-mail appeal.
